thread.title: MARKET SNAPSHOT: U.S. Stock Futures Inch Up As Apple's IPhone Event Grabs The Spotlight

author: morningstar.com
title: MARKET SNAPSHOT: U.S. Stock Futures Inch Up As Apple's IPhone Event Grabs The Spotlight
text:
By Victor Reklaitis, MarketWatch
Also on tap: producer prices, Fed's beige book
U.S. stock futures edged higher Wednesday, signaling the market could build on the prior session's rally.
Investors are due to get details on Apple Inc.'s latest iPhones, along with a reading on producer prices. They're also slated to hear from Federal Reserve officials, as well as get the central bank's beige book report.
What are the main benchmarks doing?
Dow Jones Industrial Average futures added 12 points, or less than 0.1%, to 26,014, while S&P 500 futures tacked on 1.20 points, or less than 0.1%, to 2,891. Nasdaq-100 futures rose by 14.50 points, or 0.2%, to 7,526.50.
On Tuesday, the Dow , S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite closed higher Tuesday (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/us-stock-futures-stumble-as-investors-turn-cautious-amid-september-blues-2018-09-11), with energy and telecom shares helping to lead the way up.
The three gauges have scored year-to-date advances that range from 5.1% to 15%, as of Tuesday's close.
What's driving markets?
Trade tensions between the U.S. and its partners have put pressure on global markets in recent months, but American equities have continued to get a boost from encouraging economic reports and companies' upbeat quarterly reports.
Investors this week have been tracking the fight between the U.S. and China in particular, as analysts warn that a full-blown trade war would hurt economic growth.
Don't miss:5 things about a U.S.-China trade war that might surprise investors (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/5-things-about-a-us-china-trade-war-that-might-surprise-investors-2018-09-11)
What are strategists saying?
"Apple was a notable mover in the previous session and will remain under the spotlight as investors look towards its latest product launch," said London Capital Group analysts in a Wednesday note.
Which stocks are in focus?
Shares in Apple Inc.(AAPL) rose 0.6% in premarket action ahead of its event Wednesday that is expected to deliver details about its latest iPhones -- especially how much they'll cost (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/the-biggest-mystery-about-the-new-iphones-is-the-price-2018-09-08). The stock is up 1.2% this week, as of Tuesday's close, adding to its 2018 gain of 32%.
Don't miss:Apple's event will be about more than just the iPhone (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/apples-event-will-be-about-more-than-just-the-iphone-2018-09-11)
WellCare Health Plans Inc.'s stock (WCG) could see active trading following news that the managed-care provider will join the S&P 500 (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/wellcare-health-plans-to-be-added-to-sp-500-2018-09-11), replacing XL Group Ltd.(XL) , which is being acquired French insurance giant AXA SA(CS.FR) .
Shares in T-Mobile US. Inc.(TMUS) and Sprint Corp.(S) could make moves after the Federal Communications Commission paused its 180-day clock (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/fcc-pauses-its-review-of-t-mobile-sprint-merger-2018-09-11) for reviewing the merger of the two wireless carriers.
Which economic reports are on tap?
An August report on producer prices is scheduled to hit at 8:30 a.m. Eastern Time, with economists polled by MarketWatch forecasting growth of 0.2%.
Check out:MarketWatch's Economic Calendar (http://www.marketwatch.com/economy-politics/calendars/economic)
On the Federal Reserve front, St. Louis Fed President James Bullard is due to give a speech in Chicago at 9:40 a.m. Eastern Time, and Fed Gov. Lael Brainard is expected to make remarks in Detroit at 12:45 p.m. Eastern
The central bank is slated to release its beige book at 2 p.m. Eastern.
